title: One Release for All: Private Simple Linear Regression Via Improved Simplex Mapping
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31295v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a single-release extension of DP-RSS for private simple linear regression when both input and output are bounded in $[0,1]$. Rather than privately releasing several related sufficient-statistic estimates, we encode the required information in one unit-sensitivity vector and apply the Laplace mechanism once at the full privacy budget. The required least-squares sufficient statistics are then recovered by deterministic post-processing and used directly in an ordinary least-squares solve. We obtain variance reductions of $1.67$--$2.67\times$ relative to DP-RSS for several statistics. Experiments show that the benefit is most pronounced in the high-privacy regime, while the methods converge as privacy noise becomes negligible.

title: Single-Photon Detectors for Optical Wireless Communications: A Tutorial
authors: Ziyuan Shi, Yueying Zhan, Lei Yang, Mohamed-Slim Alouini
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Photon-counting receivers extend optical wireless communication (OWC) into regimes in which only a few detected photons are available per information bit, but the detector can no longer be treated as an interchangeable ideal counter. This tutorial develops a communication-oriented, port-to-bit framework for single-photon detection in indoor, terrestrial, airborne, space, underwater, non-line-of-sight, and integrated communication-and-sensing links. It compares SPADs, silicon photomultipliers, CMOS SPAD arrays, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, PMT/MCP-PMT receivers, upconversion detectors, and emerging technologies through photon-detection efficiency, timing, active area, dynamic range, spectral coverage, readout, cooling, and integration requirements. Beginning with the ideal Poisson channel, the tutorial then develops communication-level models for dead time, recovery, finite-pixel occupancy, saturation, background counts, afterpulsing, crosstalk, nonuniformity, and event loss. These models are connected to modulation, likelihood-based detection, synchronization, channel estimation, soft decoding, and detector-aware receiver processing, with numerical studies that compare algorithms under a common detector and detectors under a common algorithm. Finally, a unified link-budget and system co-design methodology is used to relate photons per bit, sensitivity, bandwidth, data rate, and link margin, and representative demonstrations are normalized to expose practical tradeoffs. The central conclusion is that useful photon efficiency is an end-to-end property of the optical front end, detector, readout, and digital receiver, rather than a detector metric in isolation.

title: Predictive Self-Entropy in Dirichlet Universal Coding: A Factor-Two Central Limit Theorem and a Markov Extension
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31297v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sequential universal coders produce both a realized log-loss and, before each symbol is observed, a predictive distribution with its own Shannon entropy. We compare the realized arithmetic code length with the cumulative predictive self-entropy, the prequential sum of the self-expected logarithmic scores of the issued forecasts. This forecast-only quantity is neither a plug-in entropy estimate nor a posterior entropy functional. For finite-alphabet memoryless sources and Dirichlet (add-$\alpha$) sequential predictors, we prove a joint central limit theorem for the two normalized quantities. They have the same first-order entropy limit but different second-order fluctuations: for every nonuniform i.i.d. source, cumulative predictive self-entropy has exactly twice the leading asymptotic variance of realized code length, and the ordinary mean-square-error ratio converges to two. We also give its logarithmic bias coefficient. For fixed finite-order Markov sources with context-wise Dirichlet predictors, the factor-two result becomes a context/innovation covariance decomposition, recovering the i.i.d. factor two when only the innovation component contributes.

title: On the concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31326v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show that the Gaussian uniquely maximizes the $L^2$ concentration of the ambiguity function on every centered ball, up to time-frequency shifts and multiplication by a unimodular constant. The proof relies on ideas from quantum information theory.

title: Ternary Perfect $2$-Burst-Correcting Codes
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31328v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A construction for a ternary perfect linear $2$-burst-correcting code is presented for every redundancy $r \geq 5$. The construction is recursive with seeds given for $5 \leq r \leq 7$. The construction of redundancy $r \geq 8$ is derived from a code of redundancy $r-3$ and it distinguishes between codes of even and odd length.

title: Fuzzy vectors from first and second moments: Affine consistency, carrying and sparsest realizations
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31351v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When the probability law of a random vector cannot be identified, its mean and possibly singular covariance can often still be elicited. We consider fuzzy vectors with compact convex cuts as mathematically tractable representations of such a moment pair, and ask how they must be designed to rely only on this information. We postulate two modeling desiderata, independence of the choice of origin and basis, and invariance under embeddings into a higher-dimensional space. Under these requirements alone we show that, in every ambient dimension, every level set of the fuzzy vector must be a Mahalanobis ellipsoid centered at the mean. Its complete specification then amounts to the choice of a radial profile for each covariance rank. We call a fuzzy vector a carrier of the moment pair if at least one of its random-set selections has exactly the given mean and covariance. For an ellipsoidal fuzzy vector of rank $p\ge1$ with radial profile $\rho$, carrying is equivalent to $\int_0^1\rho(\alpha)^2d\alpha\ge p$, and equality characterizes the inclusion-minimal carriers within the fixed-shape Mahalanobis class. A discrete random vector with the same mean and covariance and the fewest equally weighted atoms has its atoms on a regular simplex in Mahalanobis coordinates. Completing this simplex under the rotations left free by the moments yields the minimum-volume crisp ellipsoid in the state space that carries them. The ellipsoidal representation also encodes interaction through the covariance matrix.

title: Analysis and Optimal Approximation of Operator-Valued Riccati Equations with Unbounded Control Operators
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31407v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we present new results on the well-posedness and approximation of the operator-valued Riccati equations that arise in the context of control systems with unbounded control operators, e.g. interior point and boundary control systems. We first prove that the Bochner integral form of the operator-valued Riccati equation is well-posed even if the control operator is unbounded. We then leverage the favorable structure of the Bochner integral form to prove that the error of approximate solutions are bounded by the approximation error of the process $C_0$-semigroup. This general result then leads to the correct prediction of optimal error estimates for the finite element approximation of the Riccati equation. The analysis is carried out on both the time-dependent and stationary Riccati equations and our numerical convergence study on the weakly damped wave process and the thermal process with delta function actuation operators corroborate the results of our analysis.

title: Doubly Intermittent Singular Skew Products
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31490v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study a large class of skew product systems, which can also be thought of as random dynamical systems, coupling a uniformly expanding circle map with a full branch interval map with two indifferent fixed points and unbounded derivatives. This significantly generalizes the setting of several skew products considered in the literature, in particular the Gou\"ezel skew products [Gou\"ezel, Statistical properties of a skew product with a curve of neutral points, Erg. Th. & Dyn. Sys. (2007)], in which the fibre maps are intermittency maps with a single indifferent fixed point and bounded derivatives. Through the construction of an induced full branch map, we prove various statistical properties of the skew products, including existence of an invariant probability measure equivalent to Lebesgue and decay of correlations.

title: The Work of Mathematical Production in the Age of AI
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31523v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The emergence of powerful artificial intelligence has unsettled the relationship between mathematical production and the human intellectual activity that mathematical artifacts have traditionally documented. We argue that mathematical practice cannot be adequately understood through the production of mathematical knowledge alone, and distinguish four interrelated dimensions of inquiry: knowledge, understanding, making sense, and figuring out.
  Building on Kitcher, Dewey, and subsequent philosophy of mathematical practice, we develop an expanded framework incorporating the cognitive and computational capacities of mathematical communities, their conceptual organizations, provisional investigative models, and the role of unsuccessful inquiry. We propose reconceptualizing artificial intelligence as a manifestation of physically organized computation whose mathematical behavior itself can become an object of experimental investigation.
  This perspective motivates a program of \emph{natural mathematics}, by which we mean the construction and comparison of artificial intellectual communities developing mathematical practices under different cognitive, conceptual, and normative conditions. Our aim is not simply to automate mathematical research or increase the production of theorems, but to investigate the robustness and contingency of mathematical concepts, the possibilities of alternative mathematical practices, and what such investigations might reveal about human mathematical cognition.
  Finally, we consider the future of human intellectual agency in a world where mathematical production need no longer depend upon humans. We argue for intergenerational epistemic stewardship as a justification for sustaining human mathematical traditions and opportunities for intellectual participation, independently of humanity's continued indispensability to mathematical progress.

title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31538v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".

title: Multiplicities and $k$-numerical Range
authors: Pan Shun Lau, Nancy De Menzelthe, Tin-Yau Tam
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31553v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the wedge and projection multiplicities of a point in the $k$-numerical range $W_k(A)$ of a complex matrix $A$. The representatives are decomposable wedges of orthonormal $k$-frames and rank-$k$ orthogonal projections, respectively. For $1\le k<n$, put $r=\text{dim}_\mathbb{R}\text{span}_\mathbb{R}\{I_n,H,K\}$, where $H=(A+A^*)/2$ and $K=(A-A^*)/(2i)$. We prove that every $\xi\in\text{relint} W_k(A)$ satisfies $p_{A,k}(\xi)=n^2-r+1$ and $w_{A,k}(\xi)=\binom nk$. We determine both multiplicities at every boundary point of $W_k(A)$, including non-exposed points. For complex symmetric matrices we establish lower bounds for both real multiplicities, including singular interior fibers, and obtain exact formulas for boundary points, line ranges, and commuting symmetric parts. We also relate the two multiplicities by quadratic inequalities.

title: Distributed Time-Varying Resource Allocation in Open Networks
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31560v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider the problem of distributed resource allocation over a team of agents whose active membership changes over time. Each agent's allocation evolves according to its own temporal dynamics, while a shared equality constraint couples all active agents at every instant. For the case of quadratic local objectives, we show that the optimal solution is characterized by a linear system whose coefficient matrix couples a block-tridiagonal temporal structure with a block-diagonal Laplacian capturing the time-varying communication graph. Building on this structure, we develop a distributed forward-backward sweeping algorithm in which each agent resolves its own temporal coupling through a local forward-backward sweep, while the shared resource constraint is resolved through a distributed consensus iteration that is feasible at every iteration. Under a mild diagonal-dominance condition on the temporal coupling, we establish that the optimal allocation at any fixed time converges geometrically to a stationary solution as the horizon grows, and that our distributed algorithm tracks this limit at a matching geometric rate. These results justify a memory-efficient variant of the algorithm in which each agent retains only a bounded window of past history, with the resulting approximation error decaying exponentially in the window size. We validate these theoretical guarantees through numerical simulation, confirming the predicted convergence rates under dynamically changing team membership.

title: A decoupled BDF2-type integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert system in ferromagnetic multilayers
authors: Michele Ald\'e, Dirk Praetorius, Agus L. Soenjaya
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31567v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete, linear, decoupled BDF2-type finite element integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert (SDLLG) system arising in spintronics. The SDLLG equations couple the magnetization dynamics with a diffusion equation for spin accumulation. The proposed numerical method combines a projection-free BDF2-type tangent-plane discretization of the magnetization dynamics with BDF2 time-stepping for the spin accumulation. By treating the coupling terms explicitly through extrapolation, each time step requires only two independent linear solves that can be performed in parallel. The analysis accommodates the usual exchange field and a general, possibly nonlinear, lower-order effective field. Unconditional weak convergence towards a global weak solution is shown. We also establish bounds on the deviation from the unit-length constraint. Under additional assumptions on the associated energy functional, an energy inequality for the limiting solution is obtained. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.

title: An augmented generalized factorization bound for generalized maximum-entropy sampling
authors: Ananias S. Machado, Marcia Fampa, Jon Lee, Gabriel Ponte
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31593v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Li proposed an augmented factorization upper bound for use in branch-and-bound (B&B) algorithms aimed at the maximum entropy sampling problem (MESP). This bound improves on the factorization bound for MESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. GMESP, which selects $s$ of $n$ variables so as to maximize the product of the $t$ greatest eigenvalues of the corresponding principal submatrix of the covariance matrix, is a generalization of MESP (the case $t=s$), and the factorization bound for MESP generalizes to GMESP. We extend the augmentation technique of Li to improve on the generalized factorization bound for GMESP when the input covariance matrix is positive definite. We derive fundamental properties of the augmented bound, and we develop primal--dual constructions for use within B&B. We give checkable conditions under which the relaxation can be solved in closed form, which always hold when $t=1$, at the root and at every subproblem, and a condition under which the closed-form solution is optimal for GMESP. We compare the augmented bound with the spectral bound, establishing an exact comparison for $t=1$, an improved worst-case comparison for general $t$, and sufficient conditions for the dominance of each bound over the other. Computational experiments on benchmark instances show that augmentation can substantially reduce root gaps of the generalized factorization bound, while even reducing its computational time, and that it improves the performance of B&B. Moreover, a hybrid strategy that uses the trace upper bound to prune nodes and the closed-form certificate to avoid solving the relaxation can significantly accelerate B&B when $t$ is small.

title: Service location flexibility in dynamic vehicle routing
authors: G\'erard P. Cachon, Bora Cetin, Sophie H. Yu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31596v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Parcel lockers and delivery robots let a vehicle serve customers at nearby locations. We study this service location flexibility in the dynamic traveling repairman problem, where a single vehicle may serve each demand anywhere within a radius $r$ of its location. Arrivals form a Poisson process, demand locations are independent and uniform in the unit square, and on-site service times are i.i.d. with uniformly bounded second moments, where the radius $r$ may vary across systems as the on-site load $\rho$ tends to one. In this heavy-traffic regime, the optimal mean system time is of order $(1-\rho)^{-1}(1+\min\{1/r,1/(1-\rho)\})$, compared with $(1-\rho)^{-2}$ without service location flexibility [BvR91, PFB11]. Thus, flexibility reduces the order of optimal mean system time when $r$ stays fixed or shrinks more slowly than $1-\rho$. Moreover, when $r$ is on the order of $1-\rho$ or larger, the vehicle can attain the optimal order by repeating a fixed covering route that passes within $r$ of every location. For example, the vehicle can follow a fixed grid route through parcel lockers, with customers in each square cell sharing the locker at its center.

title: Realization of expanding dynamics by a finite horizon parabolic law response
authors: Masood Shahbaz Shoukat, Luca Di Persio, Wensheng Jia
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31618v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the discrete dynamical system generated by iterating an episodic response of a population density. In each episode, the running potential is frozen at the current density, agents solve a quadratic control problem, and the terminal density is passed to the next episode. For each prescribed positive horizon $\tau$ and each $C^k$ map $F$ of finitely many Fourier moments, with $1\le k<\infty$, we construct a finite mode interaction realizing $F$ at order $\varepsilon$. In scaled coordinates, the exact parabolic response satisfies $\|T^{(d)}_{\varepsilon,\tau}-(F,S(\tau)|_{\Es_d})\|_{C^k}\le C\varepsilon$. The estimate is uniform over a full bounded infinite dimensional Sobolev fibre and needs neither Fourier truncation nor an invariant manifold. For scalar targets with disjoint expanding branches that strictly cover their convex hull, this $C^1$ control and parabolic compactness yield compact invariant sets of the exact response. These sets factor onto the full one sided shift and contain periodic densities of every least period. Nondegenerate periodic orbits continue, and hyperbolicity requires a separate strict multiplier condition. We also prove a derivative cost obstruction for nonaffine microscopic realization, a susceptibility weighted criterion for population energy designs, and the failure of exact scalar closure under nontrivial rank one feedback. The results concern designed frozen law responses, not Nash consistent mean field game equilibria or finite player limits.

title: Two-Sided Weighted-History Transfer for Abstract Systems with Infinite Memory
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31625v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove a two-sided transfer principle for second-order systems with Hilbert-valued infinite memory. The squared norm of the coupled semigroup, from a centered weighted-history space into the energy space, is bounded above and below by constant multiples of $\rho_w(t)$. Here $\rho_w(t)$ is the squared norm of the right-translation semigroup between the corresponding weighted and unweighted memory spaces. The coupled system satisfies an energy identity, a mechanical multiplier estimate and a bounded observation. The memory density has decay of order at most polynomial, and the weight is admissible. Under these hypotheses the energy is bounded by the initial norm times $\kappa(t)+\rho_w(t)$, where $\kappa$ is the tail of the kernel. The two-sided equivalence holds when $\rho_w$ is integrable and the kernel has a finite first moment and satisfies a tail bound, or when $\kappa\le C_\kappa\rho_w$. For the density $pb(1+s)^{-p-1}$, with $p>1$ and $b>0$, and the weight $(1+s)^{2\theta}$, with $\theta>0$, the rate is $(1+t)^{-\min\{2\theta,p+1\}}$. For kernels and weights with logarithmic factors, under explicit conditions on the exponents, the logarithm of the weight enters the rate below the saturation threshold, and the logarithm of the kernel enters above it. A theorem with a prescribed decay of the inherited history gives exact exponents for algebraically growing histories. The hypotheses are verified for gradient-memory waves without instantaneous damping, endpoint-damped strings, damped plates and oscillators.

title: A Kernel Framework for Linear Operator Equations
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31626v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Solving linear operator equations with nonlocal terms or heterogeneous constraints often requires specific numerical schemes. We develop a unified approach based on embedding such equations into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Differential, boundary, and integral operators are represented by their Riesz representers in the RKHS. The equations are solved in the regularized least-squares sense at finitely many collocation points. The solution is a finite linear combination of operator-induced representers and is obtained from a single linear system. Its sensitivities, such as financial Greeks, follow by direct differentiation. To reduce the computational cost for large collocation sets, we introduce a Nystr\"om approximation based on subsampling the operator-induced representers. It yields the best approximation of this solution within the reduced trial space, in a regularized empirical norm. Numerical examples cover ordinary, partial, and partial integro-differential equations, including multi-asset and jump-diffusion option pricing.

title: Sampling Error in Time-Discretized Stochastic Optimal Control
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31632v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study sampling error for Euler discretizations of stochastic optimal control problems driven by Brownian motion. For ordinary Monte Carlo sampling, the error can diverge under time refinement when empirical-mean fluctuations accumulate as bias. Under global Lipschitz assumptions and a bounded noise coefficient, we derive finite-sample bounds for the value-function error without assuming smooth value functions or independence across sampling batches. The bounds isolate the empirical-mean contribution. For convergence under time refinement, ordinary Monte Carlo generally requires the number of samples per stage to grow at a faster rate than the number of intervals in the time mesh, whereas antithetic and recentered sampling eliminate the empirical-mean term and yield error bounds uniform over meshes with a fixed sample size per stage. We establish lower bounds showing that the ordinary and antithetic sampling terms are attained. We also prove sample-size convergence for all three methods on fixed meshes. For antithetic and recentered sampling, convergence is uniform over meshes in every noise dimension, with sharp sample-size rates in dimensions at least three.

title: Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31650v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $\delta^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. Remote-history packets give residuals of order $S^{-1}$ for the truncated generator and of order $S^{-1}+h$ after discretization, improved to $S^{-1}$ at zero frequency. Numerical tests confirm the residual orders.

title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
authors: Siyad Rahman Mandottil, Neela Nataraj, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31722v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. Well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed Maxwell tensor are established under suitable regularity assumptions, in parameter-weighted norms in which the inf-sup constant is independent of the correlation length and of the permittivity ratio. The constants in the error estimates are independent of both parameters as well, up to a loss of at most half an order when the mesh does not resolve the length scale (square root of the relative permittivity); the Sobolev norms of the solution may still depend on the parameters through boundary layers. The postprocessed Maxwell stress converges with optimal order on quasi-uniform meshes, except for the lowest-order scheme in 3D. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the properties of the proposed method for problems in 2D and 3D.

title: Generating health variables for a synthetic population of Santa Catarina, Brazil, via ensemble learning and a calibrated linear program
authors: Maria Eduarda Pinheiro, Vitoria Caroline Blau
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31726v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agent-based models in epidemiology require synthetic populations with health-related attributes, which in Brazil are available only from sample surveys such as the Pesquisa Nacional de Sa\'ude (PNS). We add health variables, including smoking, alcohol consumption, physical exercise, self-rated health and chronic conditions, to a georeferenced synthetic population of the state of Santa Catarina. Class probabilities are estimated by an ensemble of logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine, and individuals are assigned to classes by a linear program that reproduces the class proportions estimated from the survey. We show that, under a mild condition satisfied by our ensemble, the penalty term of this program is no longer needed, and the proportions are reproduced exactly. In a cross-validation on PNS data, the method attains the best results.

title: Sharp Hellinger Risk of the Multivariate Gaussian NPMLE
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31728v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For multivariate Gaussian location mixtures whose mixing distributions have coordinatewise sub-Gaussian tails, we prove that the unconstrained nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator attains the minimax rate $(\log n)^d/n$ under squared Hellinger loss. This holds for every fixed dimension $d\geq2$ and every fixed tail parameter $\sigma>0$. The upper bound applies to every measurable choice of a global likelihood maximizer and improves the earlier bound of order $(\log n)^{d+1}/n$ by a factor of $\log n$.
  A key step is a sharp bracketing bound for multivariate polynomials. For the $L^2(\rho)$ unit ball of real polynomials in $d$ variables with total degree at most $m$, the log bracketing number at width $\varepsilon$ is at most $\binom{m+d}{d}\log(C_d/\varepsilon)$ for $0<\varepsilon\leq1$. The constant $C_d$ depends only on $d$. The bound holds for every positive Borel measure $\rho$ under which each nonzero polynomial in the space has a finite, positive $L^2(\rho)$ norm. We prove the bound using volume estimates for a complex Veronese cone and Gaussian small-ball probabilities, then apply it to bound the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of Gaussian mixture densities. We obtain the matching minimax lower bound by adapting the Hermite perturbation construction of Kim and Guntuboyina.

title: Verified two-sided bounds for the inf-sup constant of the divergence on planar polygons
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31734v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The inf-sup constant $\beta(\Omega)$ of the divergence governs the stability of the Stokes problem. For polygons, analytic lower bounds are far from the true value, and numerical methods either bound $\beta$ from above or require spectral-gap and mesh-fineness hypotheses that cannot presently be checked. We propose a method that produces verified lower bounds without any such hypothesis. It rests on the Friedrichs formulation of $\beta$ in the Bergman space and on a multiplier identity that controls the non-compact corner contribution pointwise, with the sharp corner constant; the remaining compact part is bounded by a finite matrix inequality that is checked in exact and ball arithmetic. We prove that the bounds converge to $\beta$. Together with enclosed Rayleigh quotients of explicit trial functions (and, for the square, the bottom $\frac12-\frac1\pi$ of the essential spectrum) this yields two-sided enclosures, e.g.\ $0.426245\le\beta\le0.426252$ for the square and $0.303973\le\beta\le0.304078$ for the L-shaped domain. For a square with a square hole, which is neither simply connected nor star-shaped, we obtain $0.154596\le\beta\le0.154781$. For the rectangles $(0,1)\times(0,r)$ we enclose $\beta$ for eight aspect ratios and prove for the five ratios $r\in\{\frac14,\frac38,\frac12,\frac9{16},\frac58\}$ that $\beta^2$ is an isolated eigenvalue below the essential spectrum; the last two lie beyond the range covered by the explicit bound of Costabel, Crouzeix, Dauge and Lafranche. As an application, the certified values give guaranteed a posteriori bounds for Taylor--Hood approximations of the Stokes equations, including the doubly connected domain, for which, to our knowledge, no explicit lower bound for $\beta$ had been available.

title: Asymptotic Normality of the Pearson Correlation between Two Weakly Dependent Random Fields
authors: Jiyue Qin, Armin Schwartzman, Samuel Davenport
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31743v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the sample Pearson correlation coefficient between two weakly dependent random fields on a lattice of any fixed dimension. Under strict stationarity, $(BL,\theta)$-weak dependence and mild moment conditions, we establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimator on regularly growing domains, which need not be rectangular, with an asymptotic variance expressed through joint fourth-order moments. When the correlation is zero, asymptotic normality holds under weaker conditions. When the fields are independent, the asymptotic variance simplifies to a sum over spatial lags of products of their autocorrelations. The variance approximations behind the classic modified $t$-test, although derived for independent Gaussian fields, target the right variance even without Gaussianity. We also give sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality that are easy to check and cover bounded, Gaussian, $m$-dependent and independent fields. For Gaussian fields, summable auto- and cross-covariances suffice. These conditions rely on new closure results. Squares and products, although not Lipschitz, preserve $(BL,\theta)$-dependence for Gaussian fields, and products of independent fields do so when one is positively or negatively associated. Finally, we propose kernel-based estimators of the asymptotic variance, enabling inference without Gaussianity or parametric spatial models. Simulation studies illustrate their finite-sample performance.

title: Joint Trajectory and Power Optimization for Movable-Antenna-Aided Secure Transmission
authors: Jiacheng Liao, Fengchao Zhu, Guojie Hu, Ying Zhang, Tong-Xing Zheng
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31768v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates joint trajectory and power optimization for movable antenna (MA)-aided secure transmission, where the MA can transmit during its movement. Specifically, the average secrecy rate is maximized subject to movement and power constraints, which couple the MA positions and transmit powers over time, respectively. To tackle this nonconvex problem, we first decouple the transmit powers via Lagrangian duality, where the optimal power for a given trajectory is derived in semi-closed form and shown to depend only on the current MA position. Accordingly, we decouple the MA positions by equivalently reformulating the problem on a discretized linear rail in terms of the farthest grid point and the number of time slots spent at each grid point. Then, from strong duality of the convex relaxation for each farthest point, we construct an asymptotically optimal solution in which the MA dwells at no more than two positions. Finally, a low-complexity dual-based branch-and-bound algorithm is developed to select the farthest grid point and certify the optimality gap. Simulation results show that the proposed design outperforms the benchmark schemes.

title: Bounds on the Distance of Subgradient Trajectories to the Optimal Set
authors: Nicholas Dwork, Charles Tsao, Jorge Balbas, Cody Coleman, John M. Pauly
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31773v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A subgradient method with a constant step size may reach a minimizer and subsequently move away from it. Thus, a bound on the best objective value does not characterize the remainder of the trajectory. In this manuscript, we first establish that the trajectory enters a near-optimal sublevel set in finitely many iterations. We then use the Hausdorff distance between this sublevel set and the optimal set to bound the distance of every subsequent iterate from the optimal set. For objectives with weak sharp minima, we derive a tighter bound and construct examples demonstrating that the bound is tight. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical results and illustrate when the bounds are conservative.

title: A Correlative-Sparse Matrix Positivstellensatz under Pointwise Commutation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31784v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The scalar Positivstellensatz adapted to correlative sparsity enables substantially smaller moment--SOS relaxations for sparse polynomial optimization. Its matrix counterpart, however, fails in general, even under the running intersection property and local Archimedean assumptions. In this paper, we establish a matrix Positivstellensatz under these assumptions and an additional pointwise commutation condition. Specifically, if a polynomial matrix admits a decomposition whose summands commute pairwise on the feasible set, then positive definiteness on this set implies membership in the sum of the local matrix quadratic modules. The proof uses central common lower envelopes to derive an integral inequality for positive matrix-valued clique measures with consistent separator marginals, without requiring these measures to admit a global extension. We apply this result to establish asymptotic convergence of the corresponding sparse moment--SOS hierarchy for polynomial matrix optimization. We also derive a criterion for finite convergence of moment relaxation and extraction of a global minimizer based on local flatness and consistency of the local representing matrix measures on overlapping variable blocks. Finally, we provide a sufficient construction of commuting decompositions through linear equations, using a reference polynomial matrix with a simple spectrum at some point.

title: A Sequential Quadratic Programming Perspective on Optimal Control
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31786v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between the iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator (iLQR), Differential Dynamic Programming (DDP), and Newton's method for optimal control problems. Using a unified Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) framework, we introduce Newton-LQR, a Riccati-based algorithm that solves for the exact Newton step the optimal control problem. Within this framework, we establish that iLQR is a principled modified SQP method rather than merely an approximation of DDP. We show that iLQR generates a descent direction, whereas the inclusion of dynamics Hessians in DDP and Newton-LQR may lead to indefinite quadratic subproblems and necessitate regularization. We further distinguish DDP and the proposed Newton-LQR algorithm through their treatment of costate information and second-order dynamics terms. Numerical experiments across six benchmark problems demonstrate that iLQR often exhibits superior convergence during the initial optimization phase, while Newton-LQR and DDP can exploit second-order information to accelerate convergence near a solution.

title: Gradient-free MCMC exploiting low-dimensional Gaussian and nonGaussian posterior structure
authors: Hongqiao Wang, Jiahua Jiang, Jing Liu, Jinglai Li
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31792v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for Bayesian inverse problems is expensive: the unknown is high-dimensional, every likelihood evaluation requires a forward solve, and gradients are often unavailable. The posterior typically differs from the prior in a few directions and is often approximately Gaussian in most of them but strongly non-Gaussian in a few. We propose the NQU sampler, a gradient-free MCMC method that splits the parameter space into non-Gaussian (N), approximately quadratic (Q) and uninformative (U) directions. The split is learned once, before sampling, from likelihood values, and each block is updated by a kernel suited to it; a collapsed update handles a global prior scale. Because the learned structure only shapes the proposals, every update leaves the exact posterior invariant, at the cost of one likelihood evaluation. We give a condition under which the blocks can be learned and show that, for likelihoods with exactly the learned structure, the spectral gap of the sampler does not depend on the dimension, whereas updating the scale given all coordinates can have a gap of order $1/d$. On the posterior axes, the NQU sampler, learning included, needed the fewest evaluations in four of five synthetic examples with $d=200$, among nine baselines including gradient-based ones; in those with non-Gaussian directions, gradient-free baselines needed at least ten times as many. On a methane ignition problem with 219 uncertain rate constants, it gave consistent estimates, whereas full-space robust adaptive Metropolis needed about 300 times as many evaluations and an ensemble sampler degenerated.

title: Viscosity Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Integro-Differential Equations with Non-Lipschitz Running Costs
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31830v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study a class of parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) integro-differential equations arising from stochastic recursive control problems with jumps. These equations involve a L\'evy-type operator and an additional nonlocal term in the running cost. The underlying backward generator satisfies a monotonicity condition with polynomial growth in the backward variable and is uniformly continuous, but not necessarily Lipschitz continuous, in the state, Brownian, jump and control variables. We establish well-posedness, comparison and stability results for the corresponding backward stochastic differential equations with jumps, and derive a dynamic programming principle for the associated recursive control problem. Using approximation arguments and the stability of viscosity solutions, we show that the value function provides a viscosity solution of the HJB integro-differential equation. We further establish a comparison principle for bounded sub- and supersolutions and uniqueness within a prescribed growth class, under an additional uniform bound on the jump amplitudes.

title: Multi-User Linear Precoder Optimization for Obfuscation-Aided Mixed Regular and Wiretap Coding
authors: Bastian Loss, Ahmad Nimr, Gerhard Fettweis
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31840v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Physical-layer security has attracted considerable research interest with the development of quantum computing. One prominent approach is wiretap coding, which exploits the channel advantage of a legitimate receiver over an eavesdropper to achieve secure communication. However, under unfavorable channel conditions, wiretap coding can significantly reduce the achievable rate compared to regular channel coding. Mixed coding alleviates this limitation by using wiretap coding to protect a short secret required for obfuscation, while the obfuscated payload is encoded using regular channel coding. In this work, we propose a generalized obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system based on the multi-user (MU)-linear precoding (LP) architecture that unifies existing approaches employing different obfuscation functions. We then formulate the corresponding precoder optimization problem, abstracting the obfuscation function through a minimum secrecy rate constraint. Numerical simulations using a geometric two-user line-of-sight (LoS) channel demonstrated how the minimum secrecy rate requirement determines the operating point of mixed coding between regular and wiretap coding. Subsequent beampattern analysis revealed a key synergy between mixed coding and precoding: Mixed coding enables individual beam shaping for the two coding layers. Finally, spatial analysis showed that mixed coding offers the largest sum-rate gains when users are positioned at similar angles.

title: Fractional Triangular Maximal Operators on Locally Finite Trees
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31845v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce and study the centered and uncentered fractional triangular maximal operators, $\mathcal{N}^\gamma$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^\gamma$, on locally finite trees. A key geometric tool that consists of a family of overlapping triangles with total measure comparable to a ball is established, which facilitates the analysis of ball-type maximal operators. Our main results include: complete pointwise comparisons among these and classical fractional maximal operators on homogeneous trees; sufficient geometric conditions and counterexamples for general trees; and sharp $\ell^p \to \ell^q$ boundedness theorems for the new maximal operators, with optimal ranges of exponents verified by counterexamples. Finally, we compare the unboundedness regions of the ball-type maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^\gamma$ and the triangular maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^\gamma$ on a prototypical tree, proving that the former's region strictly contains the latter's for all $0 < \gamma \leq 1$.

title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger systems
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31846v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pm\lambda_{1},\pm\lambda_{2}$ satisfying $0<\lambda_{1} < \lambda_{2} < 2\lambda_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.

title: Robust Estimators for Stochastic Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31853v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Derivative-free optimization (DFO) methods are popular for solving stochastic optimization problems, with model-based methods being a practically successful class of DFO algorithm. In most existing works, sufficiently accurate objective estimates (used for model construction and to test for sufficient decrease) are constructed by taking a sample mean of several noisy evaluations. In this work, we demonstrate that using robust estimators (specifically the median, trimmed mean, and median-of-means) can improve the sample complexity of model-based DFO methods. Our numerical results demonstrate that robust estimators are also a practical choice for algorithm implementations.

title: Sharp Poincar\'e-Wirtinger Inequalities on Finite Graphs
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31854v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $G_n=(V_{G_n},E_{G_n})$ be the finite connected graph with $n\geq3$ vertices. We study the sharp constant $C_{G_n,p}$ such that the Poincar\'{e}-Wirtinger inequality \[ \Vert f-m_f\Vert_p\leq C_{G_n,p} {\rm Var}_{p}^{G_n}(f) \] holds for every $f$ on $V$, where ${\rm Var}_{p}^{G_n}$ stands for the $p$-variation on $G_n$ and $m_f$ stands for the arithmetic mean of $f$. For complete graphs, the optimal constant is known for $p\in[1,3+\delta_n^1)\cup(3+\delta_n^2,+\infty)$, with $\delta_n^1=\frac{1}{2n^2\ln n}+O(1/n^3)$ and $\delta_n^2=\frac{2}{n}+O(1/n^2)$. In this paper, we firstly extend the admissible range to all $p\in(0,\infty)$. Secondly, we obtain the sharp constant $C_{S_n,p}$ for the star graph $S_n$ in the range $p\in(0,+\infty)$ and give estimates for the sharp constant $C_{P_n,p}$ on path graphs when $p\in(0,+\infty)$. Thirdly, we characterize the extremizers on complete graphs and star graphs, and establish the existence of monotone extremizers on path graphs for $p\in(0,+\infty)$. For path graphs, we obtain explicit sharp constants for $p\in(0,1]\cup\{2\}$, and interpolation upper bounds for $p\in(1,+\infty)$. We also prove that for any finite connected graph $G_n$, the best constant at $p=+\infty$ is exactly its remoteness. Moreover, for general finite connected graphs $G_n$ and $p\in(0,+\infty)$, we establish optimal bounds for $C_{G_n,p}$; the complete graph uniquely attains the lower bound for all $p>0$; the path graph attains the upper bound for $p>1$, but for $0<p\leq1$ there exist nonpath graphs that attain the same supremum. Finally, we show that our approach yields sharper upper bounds than the path-based estimates obtained via the Cheeger constant.

title: Upwind finite element approximation of the gradient blow-up time for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31859v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We analyze an upwind finite element method with piecewise linear elements for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a superquadratic gradient source term, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. On polytopal inner approximations of smooth bounded domains in dimensions $N=1,2,3$, we prove maximum-norm convergence of the numerical solution to the exact solution before gradient blow-up and convergence of gradient-threshold times to the blow-up time under explicit mesh and regularity assumptions. We also verify the regularity assumption and finite-time gradient blow-up for an example on the disk, to which the main theorem therefore applies. Numerical experiments illustrate this gradient blow-up.

title: Normal and Unitary Operators on Smooth Banach Spaces via the Duality Mapping
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31874v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This article extends the classical notions of normal and unitary operators from Hilbert spaces to smooth Banach spaces through the duality mapping. The class of normal operators introduced in this setting contains, as a special case, the self-adjoint operators on smooth Banach spaces defined via the duality mapping. We establish several characterisations of these operators and investigate their fundamental properties. In particular, we examine various spectral properties of normal operators on smooth Banach spaces. These results demonstrate that many fundamental aspects of the classical theory of normal and unitary operators on Hilbert spaces persist in the smooth Banach space setting.

title: Needlepoints in Quasi-Normed Orlicz Spaces and a Question of Kalton and Peck
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31890v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that the approachable points and the needlepoints coincide in every quasi-normed Orlicz function space on the probability interval. Their common set is either $\{0\}$ or $E_\Phi$. The proof gives a characterization by finite probability laws and also applies to Orlicz function spaces with the modular topology, without assuming $\Delta_2$. We then construct a separable real quasi-Banach space whose approachable points form a line and whose only needlepoint is zero. Every compact convex subset of this space is relatively locally convex. The construction gives a negative answer to the question of Kalton and Peck for general quasi-Banach spaces.

title: The Descriptive Complexity of Continuous Selections with Prescribed Hausdorff dimension of the Graph
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31897v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study the existence of continuous selections of set-valued functions with prescribed Hausdorff dimension of their graphs. We consider Hausdorff-continuous functions defined on the unit interval whose values are nonempty compact subsets of the real line. We prove that, for every $\beta\in[1,2]$, the collection of all such functions admitting a continuous selection whose graph has Hausdorff dimension $\beta$ is $\Sigma^1_1$-complete and hence is not Borel. Further, we show that this result holds even when the set-valued functions have totally disconnected values. Thus, we obtain a complete classification of the descriptive complexity of the existence problem for all possible Hausdorff dimensions of continuous graphs over the unit interval.

title: A General Framework for Identifying the Joint Potential Outcome Distribution through Support Restrictions
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31900v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many causal estimands depend on the joint distribution of potential outcomes, which is generally not identifiable because only one potential outcome can be observed for each unit. To obtain identification, researchers often impose assumptions such as monotonicity and exclusion restriction that constrain the support of this joint distribution. For treatments and outcomes that each take finitely many values, we define a similarity matrix whose entries count, for each pair of potential outcome strata, the number of treatments yielding the same outcome. We then prove that, under unconfoundedness, identification holds if and only if this matrix is invertible, yielding a criterion directly verifiable from the support. In addition, we derive an identification formula for the joint distribution under these support restrictions and show that an average causal estimand is identifiable if and only if its integrand admits an additive representation on the restricted support. Finally, we derive sharp testable implications of the support restriction. Our results unify and generalize a broad range of identification results in the literature.

title: Linearization for unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31911v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate global topological linearization with unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth. Under a spectral gap condition and a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, we show that the displacements of both the conjugacy and its inverse from the identity satisfy the same growth bound as the perturbation. Moreover, the conjugacy is unique within the class of maps whose displacements satisfy this bound. We obtain representations of the displacement in terms of stable and unstable orbit series that converge uniformly on any bounded set and give the inverse conjugacy by using the Banach fixed points theorem in a weighted function space.

title: Gradient Descent Achieves $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ Convergence
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31917v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a deterministic stepsize rule for gradient descent on a lower-bounded nonconvex function with Lipschitz-continuous gradient and Hessian. Classical analysis shows that a fixed stepsize guarantees a decrease of order $\varepsilon^2/L$ per update. In contrast, our rule uses a sequence of $\mathcal{O}(m)$ updates with a total stepsize of order $m^2/L$. We establish a weighted descent inequality for every prefix of the update sequence on a quadratic objective and control the error caused by Hessian variation on a general objective. This error determines the choice $m\asymp(L^2/(\rho\varepsilon))^{1/4}$ for small $\varepsilon$. We show that gradient descent with our stepsize rule finds an $\varepsilon$-stationary point within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ gradient evaluations, matching the optimal gradient-complexity guarantee.

title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean-Field Games in Hilbert Spaces and Applications
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31926v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates a class of linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games (LQ-GMFGs) in Hilbert spaces, where heterogeneous agents are distributed over large networks. A distinguishing feature of our model, compared with the model of well-studied finite dimensional LQ-GMFGs, is that the dynamics of agents are governed by infinite dimensional stochastic evolution equations (SEEs) involving an unbounded operator. The diffusion coefficients are allowed to depend on the state, the control, and the weighted state-average. In addition, the parameters in cost functionals could be indefinite. As the number of agents, $N$, tends to infinity, following the Nash certainty equivalence methodology, the solvability of the limit GMFG is reduced to that of an operator-valued Riccati equation and a GMFG equation system. The existence of a strongly regular solution to the former is characterized by an equivalent, easily verifiable condition, and the sufficient conditions are established for the solvability of the latter by applying the spectral decomposition method. Therefore a Nash equilibrium for the limit game is obtained. Under some adequate convergence assumptions, a set of decentralized strategies for the $N$-agent game is designed based on the Nash equilibrium of the limit GMFG, and the obtained strategy profile is shown to constitute an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical results are applied to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.

title: Symmetry-reduced High-index Saddle Dynamics for Saddle Point Search under Continuous Symmetries
authors: Yuanshen Lin, Jianyuan Yin, Lei Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31930v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For energy invariant under continuous symmetries, critical points may form critical manifolds, leading to degeneracy of the Hessian. In such cases, the ascent directions in high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) may include symmetry directions, making it difficult to locate saddle points of a prescribed Morse index. To address this issue, we propose symmetry-reduced HiSD (SR-HiSD) by formulating the quotient HiSD on the quotient manifold and horizontally lifting the dynamics to the ambient Hilbert space. Under suitable regularity and Morse--Bott assumptions, we establish local exponential stability of the quotient HiSD equilibria associated with the prescribed index and instability of equilibria associated with critical points of different indices. We further prove local convergence of the SR-HiSD position trajectory to a single point on the target critical orbit. Numerical algorithms with direction updates restricted to the horizontal space are developed. Numerical experiments on Morse clusters, the Onsager model, and the Landau--Brazovskii model demonstrate reliable searches for saddle points of the prescribed index and the construction of solution landscapes, together with improved computational efficiency in large-scale problems.

title: Kernel Estimates and Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund Theory in the $(k,a)$-generalized Laguerre setting
authors: Mingwei Shi, Yongsheng Han, Yu Liu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish heat and Poisson kernel estimates for $\mathfrak L=\|x\|^{2-a}\Delta_k$ in the $(k,a)$-generalized Laguerre setting, where $\Delta_k$ is the Dunkl Laplacian associated with a finite reflection group. The heat kernel is nonnegative, symmetric, and conservative, and satisfies a Gaussian bound in the orbit distance together with polynomial decay in the distance between the transformed coordinates. The Poisson kernel, obtained by subordination, satisfies corresponding size and time-derivative estimates, while $-t\partial_t p_t$ has integral zero in each variable. Motivated by these estimates, we introduce a class of $(k,a)$-Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund singular integral operators and show that $L^2_{k,a}$-boundedness implies $L^p_{k,a}$-boundedness for $1

<\infty$, together with weak type $(1,1)$ and $L^\infty$-to-$\BMO$ estimates. Finally, we establish a $T1$ theorem characterizing the $L^2$-boundedness of such operators by the conditions $T1\in BMO$, $T^*1\in BMO$, and the weak boundedness property.

title: Saddle-focus to saddle transition of 4D heteroclinic orbits resembling oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some dissipative Boussinesq systems
authors: Rezwana Razzaque Angana, Brendan Harding, Dimitrios Mitsotakis
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Oscillatory and regularized shock waves have long been studied to understand the formation and dynamics of undular bores in shallow waters, phenomena that typically arise from the interplay between dispersion, nonlinearity, and dissipation. In this work, we investigate and describe the nature and shape of traveling wave solutions that resemble oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some Boussinesq-type water wave models known as Bona--Smith systems in the presence of dissipation. The associated traveling wave equations are solutions of four-dimensional dynamical systems, leading to both computational challenges and rich structural behavior. In particular, to describe the properties of these traveling waves, we analyze heteroclinic orbits that connect two distinct equilibria, one of which undergoes a transition in the four-dimensional phase space from a saddle-focus to a saddle point as the dissipation parameter increases. This transition governs the nature of the wave profile, which evolves smoothly from an oscillatory shock wave to a regularized (non-oscillatory) shock wave. To compute such solutions, we introduce a finite-difference-based numerical method tailored for this class of problems.

title: Spontaneous Synchronization in Cellular Circadian Clocks
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31985v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study a population of identical cellular circadian oscillators, each a four-species transcription--translation feedback loop of the type analysed by Wang and Peskin, coupled by the exchange of cytoplasmic mRNA with a shared, well-mixed bloodstream at rate $\epsilon$. Simulations started from uniformly random phases show a collective damping of the mean rhythm followed by spontaneous synchronization. We show that the blood compartment tracks the population mean on the time scale $1/[N_c(\epsilon+\delta_m)]$, and that the population means obey the single-cell equations with a correction proportional to the variance $\sigma_{pn}^2$ of nuclear protein across cells; the correction is accurate only near synchrony. Deviations from the mean obey a linear system with periodic coefficients, whose leading Floquet exponent $-\kappa(\epsilon)$ is the asymptotic synchronization rate. Using the fact that the four first-order stages of the feedback loop commute, we prove that $\kappa(\epsilon)=\epsilon/4+O(\epsilon^2)$ on the limit cycle in the large-population limit. Numerically computed exponents agree with the decay rates measured in simulations to within $0.2\%$ for $5$ to $400$ cells. The approach to synchrony from an incoherent state is slower than $\kappa$, and at the weakest coupling tested the population remains in a two-cluster state. With intrinsic molecular noise, uncoupled cells lose their autocorrelation within about ten cycles, whereas coupled cells retain it and sustain a Kuramoto order parameter of $0.68$ to $0.93$.

title: Subnormality of $B$-operators of class $\mathscr{S}$
authors: Sameer Chavan, Zenon Jan Jab{\l}o\'nski, Il Bong Jung, Jan Stochel
abstract:
arXiv:2611.31997v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We characterize subnormality of $B$-operators $T=\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}V&E\\0&S\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ on $\mathcal{H}_1\oplus\mathcal{H}_2$, where $V$ is an isometry, $V^*E=0$, $S$ is subnormal, and $S|E|=|E|S$. We determine when $T$ admits compactly supported signed elementary measures and express them explicitly in terms of the elementary measures of $S$. Requiring the signed elementary measures of $T$ to be positive yields a complete measure-theoretic characterization of the subnormality of $T$. If $E$ is injective, $T$ is subnormal if and only if it is a contraction. In the general case, the subnormality of $T$ is equivalent to the contractivity of its restriction to $\mathcal{H}_1\oplus\overline{{\mathcal R}(|E|)}$. We also obtain equivalent criteria involving the Taylor spectra of $(S,|E|)$, its minimal normal and minimal quasinormal extensions, and the corresponding pairs of moduli. These results extend the characterization previously known for a quasinormal lower-right entry.

title: Driver Surge Maps for Supply Rebalancing with Downstream Matching
authors: Yida Xu, Baichuan Mo, Zhengzhong Ricky You, Yuan Zhou, Hao Yi Ong, Zuo-Jun Max Shen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.32001v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ride-hailing platforms use driver-facing surge maps to rebalance spatial supply by offering zone-level bonuses. These bonuses can reshape supply by inducing nearby drivers to relocate and encouraging latent drivers to become dispatchable, but both responses are voluntary. Within short decision windows, platforms risk offering bonuses that reshape driver supply without generating sufficient downstream matching value to justify the associated payments. We formulate the driver surge map design problem (DSMDP) to optimize zone-level bonuses while anticipating voluntary driver responses and downstream matching. To assess how bonus adjustments affect net operating profit, we conduct a marginal analysis that identifies when small bonuses improve on the no-bonus map and how spatial smoothness links bonus decisions across zones. Using these marginal values, we develop an iterative solution approach (ISA) to sample dual sensitivities of the matching linear program across nearby matching regimes and guide real-time bonus updates. Theoretical analysis provides certificates of approximate stationarity and establishes conditions for stationary limits. Computational experiments show that ISA improves net operating profit over the best-performing feasible benchmark by up to 19.37% on the generated instances and by up to 8.43% in the New York City study. Local shortage alone is not a sufficient basis for bonus allocation. Platforms should target responsive supply whose downstream matching value justifies the associated bonus payments. Latent-driver activation can support higher-value matches even when all demand is served, but the resulting gains must also cover additional payments to drivers who would already be matched without incentives. Results indicate diminishing returns to bonus spending and show that moderate spatial smoothness can preserve most of the gains from spatial targeting.
